LESSON: WRITING 5.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING - NARRATIVE COMPOSITIONS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing - Narrative Compositions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing - Narrative Compositions, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we organise ideas in our compositions? 2. How can you make your writing interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  In purposive groups, identify the parts of a narrative composition,  In purposive groups work with peers to plan a narrative composition of about 160-200 words,  In purposive groups read sample narrative compositions with peers and critique them for: - correctness of language - flow or organisation of ideas - relevance to the topic - creativity  Use the steps of the writing process to create a narrative composition of about (160 -200 words), on tourist attraction sites. Learners with manipulation difficulties could be purposively grouped/ paired/ individually to write/ stamp/ mount. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  In purposive groups, identify the parts of a narrative composition,  In purposive groups work with peers to plan a narrative composition of about 160-200 words,  In purposive groups read sample narrative compositions with peers and critique them for: - correctness of language - flow or organisation of ideas - relevance to the topic - creativity  Use the steps of the writing process to create a narrative composition of about (160 -200 words), on tourist attraction sites. Learners with manipulation difficulties could be purposively grouped/ paired/ individually to write/ stamp/ mount. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing - Narrative Compositions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication: The learner’s ability to communicate effectively is developed as they practise the skills of writing clearly

by following the stages of the writing process and creating a narrative composition.

 Creativity and Imagination: The learner’s artistic skills are enhanced as they create and write narrative compositions.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is displayed as the learner collaborates with peers to plan a narrative composition.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental education: The learner interacts with information on tourist attraction sites when creating a narrative

composition using the steps of the writing process thereby grasping knowledge on the environmental.

Link to other Subjects

The learner is able to relate the concept of the writing process to their learning in Kiswahili.
